work.text: The point is that one sees things at different moments with different eyes. Differently in the morning then in the evening. The way in which one sees also depends on one's mood … It's not the chair that should be painted, but what the person has felt at the sight of it

moment.text: No longer shall I paint interiors with men reading and women knitting. I will paint living people who breathe and feel and suffer and love.

moment.text: Munch was enthralled by the vast display of modern European art, including the works of three artists who proved influential: Paul Gauguin, Vincent van Gogh, and Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec—all notable for how they used color to convey emotion.

matters.text: In December 1889 his father died, leaving Munch's family destitute. He returned home and arranged a large loan from a wealthy Norwegian collector when wealthy relatives failed to help, and assumed financial responsibility for his family from then on.
I live with the dead—my mother, my sister, my grandfather, my father...Kill yourself and then it's over. Why live?

source.author: Edvard Munch
source.title: From his notes, quoted in “Edvard Munch”

matters.text: Painted in his rented room at Saint-Cloud, outside Paris, in the months after his father's death, the picture shows a top-hatted figure sitting in the blue dark beside a window — a mood rather than an event.
